To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the elevated deoxycorticosteroine (DOC) levels in congenital adrenal hypoplasia are due to a combination of zona fasciculatas (ZF) production and zona glomerulos (ZG) stimulation.

the elevated deoxycorticosteroine (DOC) in CAH is a result of the increased 11-deoxycorticosterone production in the zona fasciculatus (ZF) and is not due to increased renin activity as in the normal zona glomerulosa.

DOC levels are increased in all subtypes of CAH, that the DOC levels in 17 alpha-hyroxyase deficiency are produced in part by renin stimulation, and that DOC production is not unique to the CAH subtypes but is seen in other conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the mineralocortoids in CAH.
the mineralocorticoids in CAH and other conditions with dissociation of cortisol from DOC.
the regulation of the ZF DOC production in CAH and the relationship of DOC to cortisol.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the elevated DOC in CAH is not a result of the increased ACTH but a result of an increased 21-deoxy steroid substrate.
DOC is the major mineralocorticoid in CAH and is responsible for the hypertension and electrolyte abnormalities in the 17 alpha-, 11 beta-, and 21-hydroxy-lase deficiency states.
the mineralocorticoids are a significant factor in the hypertension in all three major subtypes, and the DOC production in 21-hyroxyalse deficiency is not unique to this subtype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the absence of 11 beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, the ZF 17-deoxy-steroid (DOC) is the major mineralocorticoid.
the ZF DOC is a significant contributor to mineralocorticoid excess in all subtypes of CAH.
the mineralocorticoids in CAH are not a simple matter of a single hormone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DOC production is increased in the ZF and is the main cause of mineralocorticoid effects in all three subtypes of CAH.
the ZF and DOC are important components of CAH and other disorders and that they are important in the development and treatment of hypertension in CAH.
there are unique mineralocorticoid characteristics in CAH that are not seen in other forms of mineralocorticoid excess.
